questions: Are you currently taking any medications that affect your eyes, such as Botox or muscle relaxants?
Did this eye movement problem start suddenly, like after a specific event or illness?
Do you have double vision when looking straight ahead?
Have you had any recent head trauma or injury?
Do you have a history of diabetes or high blood pressure?
Is the inability to move your eyes to the side constant, or does it come and go?
orders: Bedside assessment of extraocular movements in all directions of gaze, including saccades and pursuit
Assessment for convergence-retraction nystagmus on attempted upgaze or convergence
Pupillary examination with light and near response testing
Fundoscopy to evaluate optic disc appearance
Neurological examination focusing on vertical gaze, facial sensation, and cerebellar function
MRI of the brain with attention to the midbrain and dorsal pons
Serum acetylcholine receptor antibodies and anti-MuSK antibodies
served: acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies
results: 1. Bedside assessment of extraocular movements in all directions of gaze, including saccades and pursuit
smooth pursuit and saccades: opsoclonus - chaotic multidirectional saccades without intersaccadic intervals
2. Assessment for convergence-retraction nystagmus on attempted upgaze or convergence
3. Pupillary examination with light and near response testing
pupil size and light reaction: equal and reactive
4. Fundoscopy to evaluate optic disc appearance
5. Neurological examination focusing on vertical gaze, facial sensation, and cerebellar function
cranial nerve examination: opsoclonus; otherwise normal
facial dysmorphism and general examination: unremarkable
6. MRI of the brain with attention to the midbrain and dorsal pons
MRI brain with DWI: no acute findings
7. Serum acetylcholine receptor antibodies and anti-MuSK antibodies
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Paraneoplastic opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome (likely secondary to occult breast carcinoma)
Alternative 1: Idiopathic post-infectious opsoclonus
Alternative 2: Toxic-metabolic opsoclonus
